title: Legacy root-level code & old stacks
purpose: The repo root holds the first-generation 'AUNTII' offline helpdesk robot stack: a presence-triggered voice loop (assistant_loop.py) built on standalone STT/TTS/TTT services, a root-level config module, and an older in-memory conversation/session package. It also holds the developer-facing surface that exercises the modern src stack: a CLI chat (chat.py), a CustomTkinter desktop GUI (helpdesk_gui.py), a camera profiler (profile_camera.py), and end-to-end diagnostics plus validation/audit harnesses (diag_*.py, validate_production.py, audit_production.py). Most of these are legacy or dead code superseded by src/campus_helpdesk/, but the diagnostics and validation harnesses actively boot src components (create_rag_pipeline, RAGChatService, build_production_runtime, EventBus/FSM) to verify them. The benchmark.py file named in scope does not exist at the repo root.

files.purpose: Legacy CLI robot loop that turns a camera face detection into a full voice conversation: greet on arrival, record until silence, then STT -> TTT -> TTS.

terms.definition: Speech-to-text: converting recorded microphone audio into text via the root-level stt_service.py (faster-whisper).
Text-to-speech: converting reply text into audio played through the speaker via tts_service.py.
Text-to-text: the reply-generation step (in this legacy stack, routing English to RAG and hi/kn to canned FAQ answers).
Root-mean-square amplitude of an audio chunk, compared against a threshold to detect speech vs. silence for early stop of recording.
Camera-based face detection (OpenCV Haar cascade here) that fires arrival/departure callbacks to start/stop the assistant session.

When Whisper detects a language correctly but emits it in the wrong unicode script (e.g. Kannada speech written as Devanagari); this file replaces the garbled text with a placeholder label while passing raw text to TTT.

Imports root-level services directly (presence_service, stt_service, tts_service, ttt_service). Runs one daemon thread per session guarded by a busy lock. _warmup_ollama reaches into ttt.rag_service private attrs via a getattr fallback chain, then falls back to raw ollama.Client. Silences warnings and several loggers globally.

files.purpose: Camera-based presence detection using OpenCV's built-in Haar cascade face detector on a background thread, firing on_person_arrived / on_person_left callbacks.

terms.definition: Watching a camera for a face every CHECK_INTERVAL seconds and firing arrival once per appearance, then absence after ABSENCE_TIMEOUT seconds with no face.
OpenCV's built-in XML face classifier (haarcascade_frontalface_default.xml), used here because it needs no model download and runs cheaply on a Pi CPU.
Fallback state when the cascade file or VideoCapture is unavailable; the watcher idles without detection instead of crashing.

files.notes: Legacy; the src robot stack replaces this with camera_service.py + vision_service.py (which has MockPersonDetector / confirmation-window logic). Uses CAP_V4L2 on Linux, CAP_DSHOW on Windows. Polls every CHECK_INTERVAL (1s) rather than per-frame. Standalone __main__ manual test included.

files.purpose: Offline speech-to-text via faster-whisper (Whisper 'small', CPU, int8) with language detection constrained to a candidate list {en, hi, kn}.

terms.definition: Running Whisper's detect_language(), then picking the highest-probability language from a small supported set {en,hi,kn} instead of trusting free-form detection (which hallucinates languages like 'nn' or 'ta').
int8 compute type for the Whisper model, trading negligible accuracy for ~4x faster CPU inference and much lower RAM on a Pi.
Whisper's built-in voice-activity-detection option that skips non-speech segments during transcription (optional, off in the live mic path here).
Whisper decoding beam width (5), the number of candidate hypotheses considered when decoding.

files.notes: Legacy; superseded by src/services/stt_service.py (robot stack) which uses a MockTranscriptionBackend. Singleton via __new__ so the model loads once. Contains an environment workaround: if faster_whisper import fails with DLL load / AppLocker / policy errors, it injects a fake 'av' module into sys.modules and retries. Known limitation: Kannada utterances are occasionally written in Devanagari script (safety net lives in ttt_service.py).

files.purpose: Offline text-to-speech with two tiers: instant playback of pre-rendered WAVs from tts_cache/ and live CPU synthesis via Piper (EN) and Meta MMS-TTS VITS (HI/KN), with a sine-tone fallback.

terms.definition: Deterministic WAV cache: a filename built from language + slugified text + first 8 hex chars of an md5 of the text, so repeated phrases play back instantly without synthesis.
A fast CPU neural TTS engine intended for English in this tier, but the implementation here is effectively a stub.
Meta's multilingual VITS text-to-speech (facebook/mms-tts-hin, facebook/mms-tts-kan) used for Hindi and Kannada synthesis.
contains_script() checks whether text actually contains Devanagari (hi) or Kannada (kn) unicode ranges; a mismatch routes to English Piper.

files.notes: Legacy; superseded by src/services/tts_service.py (robot stack). _synthesize_piper is a stub: it imports pyttsx3 but then just synthesizes a 523.25 Hz sine tone, and the final fallback is a 440 Hz tone, so 'Piper' produces no real speech. MMS models attempt local_files_only=True first, then fall back to downloading. CACHE_DIR is hardcoded to 'tts_cache' with no env override.

files.purpose: Text-to-text reply generation: English queries route to the production RAG pipeline (FAISS + Ollama) with fast intent pre-checks, while Hindi/Kannada use a strict canned FAQ matcher (entity + attribute regex) with an honest English fallback phrase.

terms.definition: Text-to-text: the reply-generation step that takes recognized user text and produces the assistant's answer.
For hi/kn, answers come only from a small set of human-verified FAQ strings, guaranteeing zero hallucination at the cost of coverage.

Regex checks that require both a subject entity (e.g. library/admissions) and the specific attribute asked about (location/hours/email/phone/apply); missing either routes to the English fallback phrase.
An honest reply asking the user to ask in English for detailed information, returned when an Indic query has no canned match.

files.notes: Legacy; superseded by the src application/services stack. get_reply calls rag_service.respond(user_text) without a session_id, using the default session. If RAG init fails, English falls back to greeting/time detection then a static helpdesk summary. Time queries answered with round_time_to_5_min (rounded to nearest 5 minutes). Docstring mentions qwen2.5:1.5b while the config default model is qwen2.5:3b.

files.purpose: One-off script that walks the archived scraped markdown knowledge base and prints quality metrics: exact and near-duplicates, empty/tiny/oversized files, missing metadata/titles, PDF artifacts, nav noise, broken markdown.

terms.definition: Documents differing only in whitespace/punctuation, detected by hashing the alphanumeric-only lowercase text and grouping by that normalized hash.
The count of unique documents after deduplication (len of the normalized-hash grouping), the target for a clean knowledge base.
OCR/scanner remnants such as 'Page X of Y', 'Scanned by', 'CamScanner', or excessive blank lines that indicate poor source conversion.
The '---' YAML header expected at the start of each markdown file; files without it are counted as missing metadata.
Repeated website navigation/menu boilerplate ('Home | About | Contact', 'Skip to content') left in scraped pages.

files.notes: One-off audit script against the legacy archive knowledge base; prints results only, writes nothing. Uses md5 hashes for duplicate detection. Superseded by the canonical src ingest (markdown_chunker) which has its own dedup.

files.purpose: Second version of the markdown knowledge-base duplicate analysis, using a more aggressive semantic signature hash (strips URLs, headers, source boilerplate) and reporting potential size savings from deduplication.

terms.definition: An md5 of the text after stripping URLs, markdown headers, and 'Source URL'/'Source' boilerplate, so near-duplicate content with different headers still groups together.
Estimated bytes recovered by keeping only the first file of each duplicate group (summed sizes of the remainder).

files.notes: One-off audit script, prints only. Tracks tiny (<1KB) and oversized (>100KB) files in lists instead of counts. Specifically counts duplicate groups involving 'programs_' files. Dead/legacy; not part of the modern ingest path.

files.purpose: End-to-end RAG retrieval audit: loads the FAISS index, rebuilds BM25 from its docstore, runs hybrid (RRF/weighted) retrieval, cross-encoder reranking, and ConfidenceEngine evaluation against a fixed set of test queries.

terms.definition: The dense vector index (faiss) whose L2 distances scale 0-2 and are used for dense retrieval.
A sparse lexical ranking function over the same documents, used for keyword-based retrieval.
Combining BM25 and FAISS results, here with fusion_mode 'weighted_hybrid' and weights 0.5/0.5 over bm25_top_k=25 and dense_top_k=25.
A sentence-transformers cross-encoder that re-scores the top-N retrieved documents; its score is stored as a negative distance so higher is better.
Evaluates retrieval quality (top reranker score, top distance) into a confidence score/level and an accept/reject decision (accepted when score>=0.35 or top_reranker>=0.1 or top_distance<=1.2).

config: hardcoded bm25_top_k=25, dense_top_k=25, final_top_k=25, rrf_k=60, weight_dense=0.5, weight_sparse=0.5, fusion_mode='weighted_hybrid', top_n=25, top_m=5
files.notes: Debug/audit tool, prints only. Touches private internals: faiss_store._store.docstore._dict, faiss_store._store.index.ntotal, reranker._model_loaded, and manually sets hybrid._bm25_indexed = True to bypass the normal indexing flag. Documents that CE score is stored as -distance.

files.purpose: Production validation harness that boots the exact SystemRuntime used by helpdesk_gui.py, attaches read-only EventBus and FSM observers, runs a soak test with an optional automated interaction simulator, and writes validation_log.json + validation_report.txt.

terms.definition: Running the full runtime for an extended period (default 1800s) while sampling FSM transitions, events, memory, CPU, thread count, and latency.
A callback registered with the state machine (register_on_transition) that records every state change and its timestamp.
Three or more camera disconnect events within 2 seconds, flagged as an instability blocker.
Windows Smart App Control, which blocks native DLLs such as faster-whisper and Piper; the report labels missing STT/TTS as 'BLOCKED (SAC)' environmental blockers rather than code bugs.
The 95th-percentile latency used alongside averages when reporting LLM/RAG/TTS/total turn latencies.

config: argparse --simulate (enables the automated interaction simulator thread)
output files validation_log.json and validation_report.txt (repo root)
files.notes: Explicitly a pure observer; does not modify production code. Writes artifacts to the repo root. Boots build_production_runtime(use_mock=False). The simulator publishes synthetic events (PERSON_DETECTED, VOICE_STARTED/STOPPED, TRANSCRIPT_FINAL, PERSON_LEFT) including a mock audio path 'mock.wav', and sleeps ~15s per simulated question. Default soak of 1800s is long; use --simulate for automated runs.

When the active thread count after runtime.shutdown() does not drop back to the pre-start level, detected in phase_startup.
The number of VideoCapture handles held at once; must equal exactly 1 to avoid camera ownership leaks.
A question unrelated to the knowledge base (e.g. 'Who invented gravity?') that the RAG layer should refuse or answer with low confidence.
The re-scoring model imported in phase_rag to check that reranking is available (imports from infrastructure.rag.reranker or sentence_transformers).

files.purpose: Legacy Ollama LLM wrapper over the official Python SDK with a response cache, connection checking, exponential-backoff retries tuned for model cold-load, and a streaming generator.

terms.definition: Retry delay that multiplies each attempt (10s -> 20s -> 40s -> 80s, backoff_factor=2.0, max_retries=4) to ride out model cold-load.
The first inference after a model loads weights into VRAM, which can take 60-120s on a 4GB GPU; the retry policy and keep_alive='10m' exist to tolerate it.
Ollama option keeping the model resident in memory for 10 minutes between calls to avoid reloads.
A capped (200-entry) dict keyed by stripped prompt text so repeated identical prompts return instantly.
generate_stream yields tokens incrementally for low-latency UI responses; it logs first-token latency but does not retry on failure.

data_flow: The legacy voice stack is self-contained: presence_service.py watches the camera and calls back into AssistantLoop, which records audio via sounddevice, transcribes via stt_service (faster-whisper), generates a reply via ttt_service (English -> src RAGChatService/FAISS+Ollama; hi/kn -> canned FAQ), and speaks via tts_service. The diagnostics and validation layer drives the modern src stack instead: chat.py, helpdesk_gui.py, diag_e2e.py, diag_rag.py, diag_ollama.py, profile_camera.py, validate_production.py, and audit_production.py all inject 'src/' onto sys.path and consume production components (create_rag_pipeline, RAGChatService, SessionManager, OllamaLLMService, build_production_runtime, EventBus, RobotStateMachine). helpdesk_gui.py and validate_production.py subscribe to the EventBus and FSM and publish synthetic events; audit_production.py runs pytest and validate_production.py as subprocesses and consumes their artifacts (validation_report.txt, benchmark_eval_15_results.json). Nothing in src imports these root scripts; the dependency is one-way from root into src.
external_deps: torch + transformers (Meta MMS-TTS VITS models for hi/kn)
piper-tts / pyttsx3 (Piper is effectively a stub here)
risks: benchmark.py listed in the scope does not exist at the repo root; any reference to a root benchmark script is stale.
conversation/ package is broken dead code: session.py imports conversation_manager.py which does not exist, so the package cannot be imported at all.
tts_service._synthesize_piper is a stub that emits a 523.25 Hz sine tone instead of real Piper/pyttsx3 speech; only the MMS-TTS path produces real audio, and the final fallback is a 440 Hz tone.

Duplicate competing implementations of STT, TTS, LLM, and session/memory across the root scripts and src/ create maintenance drift; the root versions are marked legacy and superseded by src counterparts.

Diagnostics reach into private internals (faiss_store._store.docstore._dict, faiss_store._store.index.ntotal, service._rag_pipeline, ttt.rag_service._llm_service, reranker._model_loaded, hybrid._bm25_indexed), making them fragile against refactors.
diag_e2e.py imports 'services.query_normalizer' and 'services.intent_router' (root-level module paths) which are not present in the current layout, so it will fail to import.
helpdesk_gui.py push-to-talk publishes VOICE_STARTED/VOICE_STOPPED bus events without itself capturing audio, so transcription relies entirely on the runtime VAD/STT path being live.
validate_production.py defaults to an 1800s soak and reports Windows SAC (Smart App Control) DLL blocking of faster-whisper/Piper as environmental blockers; its simulator sleeps ~15s per question.
helpdesk_gui_new.py is an empty stub ('# test'), which could mislead a developer into running a nonexistent GUI.
chat.py reuses rag_search_limit as max_history_turns and uses a single hardcoded 'cli' session id; /health reaches into a private _rag_pipeline attribute.
